chapters.summary: Iman Ramawi-Doster, Senior Community Organizer at New York Lawyers for the Public Interest, testifies about the severe impact of snow and ice on people with disabilities. She describes being unable to leave her home and calls for a holistic approach including assistance for seniors and disabled residents, increased fines for non-compliant businesses, and better interagency communication.
chapters.title: Iman Ramawi-Doster testifies on snow barriers for disabled New Yorkers

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: I'm going to begin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: All right, wonderful.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: Oh, afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: My name is Iman Ramawi-Doster, and I'm Senior Community Organizer for the Disability Justice Program at New York Lawyers for the Public Interest.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to present today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: NOPI's Disability Justice Program works on, among other issues, reducing barriers for people with disabilities around New York City, including by supporting those seeking better access to sidewalks, curb cuts, transportation, and businesses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: Last winter, snow and ice was especially brutal for those of us with physical disabilities and chronic illness.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: As an above and below knee amputee with lupus, which causes chronic pain and chronic fatigue, navigating the city is already difficult.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: Adding snow and ice makes it even harder.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: My husband, who doesn't have a physical disability, had to travel with me for three days after the first few snowstorms because we knew that my metal legs and walker and wheelchair were no match for the ice and the snow.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: And I couldn't even leave the house on the second day of the storm.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: How can the city talk about how much it wants disabled New Yorkers to work, but not make sure the city is set up for us to get around?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: Getting to work isn't just about transportation or workplace accommodations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: It's about making sure the streets, sidewalks, and curb cuts are clear for us in every borough.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: In addition, there are many other things we're missing out on besides work, like school, doctor's appointments, cultural events, dinner with friends, and so much more.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: These issues are not minor inconveniences.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: They're actually immediate threats to public safety and a violation of disabled New Yorkers'rights to access streets and sidewalks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: We need a holistic, intersectional, proactive, and intentional...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: approach, including implementing of the following.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: Assisting seniors and persons with disabilities with snow removal, help incentivize property owners who are unable to meet their snow obligations, assess fines for non-compliant property owners and businesses, evaluate weather current

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: And I'll submit the rest of it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: You can finish your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: Oh, sure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: Consider increasing fines for businesses, especially chain businesses, with progressive fines for repeat offenders, such as proposed in 0020-2002.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: Eliminate fines for seniors and persons with disabilities who fail to comply with snow removal mandates.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: Prioritize areas for particular importance, like areas around curb cuts and crosswalks, as well as areas with less likely to be cleared, such as sidewalks and vacant lots.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: Hire temporary workers to clear crosswalks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: Establish a youth program, such as the Summer Youth Employment, to engage with citywide snow removal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: Reimburse property owners.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: Institute uniform guidance and consider expanding the standards for clear paths.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: And of course, accountability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: Improve interagency communication among relevant agencies and incentivize them to work more cooperatively.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: For example, if there's a park across the street from a public school, one agency could clear both.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: Rate how individual DSNY districts are doing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: by utilizing daily surveys.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: And communication.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: Establish a DSNY alert system for building superintendents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: And learning from other cities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: Fines can be assessed on per daily basis rather than per violation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: Chicago, for example, fines noncompliant businesses up to $1,000 per day for the violation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: Thank you so much, and I'll sip in my testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Iman Ramawi-Doster
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Elizabeth Valdez, systems advocate at the Brooklyn Center for Independence of the Disabled, testifies that people with disabilities were trapped by snowstorms. She supports Intro 1042 but says it must be amended to track barriers like blocked curb cuts and sidewalks, and urges the city to take ultimate responsibility for clearing sidewalks and curb cuts.
chapters.title: Elizabeth Valdez testifies on inaccessible snow clearing for disabled residents

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: My name is Elizabeth Valdez, and I am the systems advocate at the Brooklyn Center for Independence of the Disabled and the Wheelchair User.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: Earlier this year, people with disabilities across the city experienced a devastating and lengthy barrier to access from the snowstorms that occurred in January and February.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: We were trapped.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: The sidewalks, streets, crosswalks, curb cuts, and bus stops were completely impassable for many of us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: We have a right to be part of our communities, a right to have jobs, a right to travel freely, a right to be part of the life of this city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: All of those rights were taken away by the city's failed response to these snowstorms.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: This committee must confront how the city's current snow clearing plans do not work for everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: Cleared streets, sidewalks, and crossings that are

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: passable by able-bodied people were not passable by people with disabilities and

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: older adults.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: In some cases, the city's efforts to clear streets for cars push snow and ice into the crosswalks and curb cuts, making it more difficult for people with disabilities to leave their homes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: We support the idea of Intro 1042.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: Before you today, but it must be amended to track barriers that impact people with disabilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: The city must track and resolve blocked curb cuts, sidewalks, crosswalks, and other areas of passage for people with disabilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: The city must also coordinate snow clearance among agencies, including at the MTA, and provide a way for people with disabilities

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: stuck by the snow to easily get help.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: Finally, we urge this committee to acknowledge the city's ultimate responsibility for the clearance of sidewalks and curb cuts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: We know and the city knows that property owners are not meeting their responsibility to keep sidewalks and curb cuts clear.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Elizabeth Valdez
utterances.text: The city must step in to meet its legal obligations and clear these barriers for people with disabilities.

chapters.summary: Mary Arnold testifies about garbage in snow piles and broader DSNY failures, including the export of 85% of the city's waste by rail. She cites environmental and health harms, violations of state law, and asks what DSNY will do to achieve compliance and protect community health.
chapters.title: Mary Arnold testifies on garbage and snow pile issues and waste export

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Arnold
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Arnold
utterances.text: Garbage in snow piles is a concern, but DSNY is also failing to keep garbage out of neighborhoods in other seasons.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Arnold
utterances.text: 85% of the city's MSW is exported to landfills and incinerators by rail.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Arnold
utterances.text: Harms include the nauseating stench from punctured and otherwise defective cans that are not leak-proof, don't seal, and sit around in neighborhoods.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Arnold
utterances.text: The rats that move through neighborhoods attracted by waste management's stinking rail cans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Arnold
utterances.text: Residents'loss of use and enjoyment of their property.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Arnold
utterances.text: Lack of achievement of DSNY's purported goals in the draft solid waste management plan for an increase in diversion.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Arnold
utterances.text: The fact is that these rates are going down.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Arnold
utterances.text: 40% of waste exported is rotting organics, and DSNY's planned empire bins and automated pickup will simply mask this failure, which fuels climate change

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Arnold
utterances.text: and spreads environmental injustice and pollution.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Arnold
utterances.text: The rapidly rising MSW export cost to New York City taxpayers, which has

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Arnold
utterances.text: to the current affordability crisis for New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Arnold
utterances.text: Lack of sealed leak-proof MSW containment is a violation of New York's Consolidated Laws Environmental Conservation Law 27-0712.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Arnold
utterances.text: The idea that DSNY's current waste by rail equipment, operations, and enforcement are adequate to maintain sealed leak-proof containment is patently false.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Arnold
utterances.text: Reports of stinking trains started in April of this year when it was 50 degrees outside and continue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Arnold
utterances.text: DSNY told you at a hearing, Chair Sanchez, that waste export by rail costs this much because DSNY does it right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Arnold
utterances.text: They do not.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Arnold
utterances.text: What is DSNY going to do now to achieve compliance with state law and their own contract requirements?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Arnold
utterances.text: Stop letting companies they do business with externalize their cost at residents'expense and protect community and environmental health.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Arnold
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Arnold
utterances.text: I know you know from personal experience what a terrible thing this is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Arnold
utterances.text: Thank you.

summary: Committee on Sanitation and Solid Waste Management held an oversight hearing on the city's snow removal and winter storm response, plus Intro 1042 on snow plowing data publication.
Council members questioned DSNY officials on pedestrian ramp clearing, bike lane plowing, equipment readiness, and coordination with other agencies.
Public testimony highlighted the impact of snowstorms on disabled New Yorkers and called for better accessibility and enforcement.
title: Committee on Sanitation and Solid Waste Management
topic: Oversight - City’s Snow Removal and Winter Storm Response
